While diffusion-based imputation models generate plausible trajectories under random missingness, they suffer from high sampling latency and lose global periodic coherence when entire sensor blocks drop out consecutively. model_response_en: Recovering missing sensor observations is essential for reliable downstream monitoring in industrial and clinical time series. While diffusion-based imputation models generate plausible trajectories under random missingness, they suffer from high sampling latency and lose global periodic coherence when entire sensor blocks drop out consecutively. We present FlowImp, a conditional flow-matching framework that reconstructs contiguous missing blocks in three ODE solver steps. Specifically, FlowImp anchors straight transport paths on observed spectral priors and enforces cross-channel phase consistency via a lightweight Fourier regularizer. Across six multivariate benchmarks under 50% block missingness, FlowImp reduces imputation MAE by 19.3% compared with CSDI while accelerating inference by 24x.

model_response_en: Recovering missing sensor observations is essential for reliable downstream monitoring in industrial and clinical time series. While diffusion-based imputation models generate plausible trajectories under random missingness, they suffer from high sampling latency and lose global periodic coherence when entire sensor blocks drop out consecutively. Specifically, FlowImp anchors straight transport paths on observed spectral priors and enforces cross-channel phase consistency via a lightweight Fourier regularizer. Across six multivariate benchmarks under 50% block missingness, FlowImp reduces imputation MAE by 19.3% compared with CSDI while accelerating inference by 24x.
